reviewEvidence:
Approved against revision-616b9536, the final sealed revision of this task. The change closes the three gaps a
command-routing assessment named — host-run visibility, a reverse routing guard, and a container picker — and it
has been reviewed by TWENTY-TWO independent fresh-context adversarial passes (per-revision passes plus the kata
verify and review nodes, each bound to a frozen brief and recorded through the adversarial gate), across 16 sealed
revisions. Roughly seventy findings were raised and every one was either fixed in code or recorded as a
deliberate, documented limitation.

WHAT IT DELIVERS
- AC-1: the session's host-command attempt count and the programs it named are visible in `/devcontainer status`,
  and the first attempt is announced on the operator channel, with an honest statement of whether a record was
  written. No command text is stored or rendered: every surface (the ledger, the runner's notice and the WITHHELD
  path's notice) renders through one enforced `displayProgram` — the first whitespace-delimited token of argv[0],
  redacted with the audit rules, then reduced to the HOST of whatever the token looks like, control characters
  stripped, capped at 64, never blank — because a program name CAN be credential-shaped and argv[0] CAN be a whole
  command line. The audit trail remains the authoritative record.
- AC-2/AC-3: `devcontainer_exec` refuses an argv element that names the HOST workspace path when the configuration
  maps it elsewhere, with a typed `policy-denied` naming the container path to use, audited as a denial with command
  identity; skipped with no mapping, for a same-path mapping, and for a container path nested under the host path.
  The match is path identity at a real segment boundary (root included) and deliberately does not inspect routed
  shell text.
- AC-4: `/devcontainer use` offers a container picker (id, state, image) from both entry points and binds exactly
  the picked candidate INCLUDING its own state; candidates are ordered running-first, so Docker's listing order
  never decides.
- AC-5: the host-escape gating asymmetry is documented as deliberate, with its reasoning, the compensating controls
  and the exact scope of the audit-side redaction; a withheld attempt is documented as never reaching the runner.
- AC-6: no regression — the CLI still receives the HOST workspace path, no argv shape changed, discovery stays
  lazy/read-only/bounded, targets are never auto-started, `stop`/`remove` keep both gates, host execution stays
  withheld-able with unchanged operation/initiator/capture defaults, `/devcontainer setup` is untouched, and the
  audit shape and modes are unchanged.

WHAT THE REVIEWS BOUGHT (they all shipped fixed)
Blocking/major findings, in the order they were found: the picker was unreachable when the ambiguous workspace was
not the only match; the operator notice and the ledger could render a credential (four separate leaks); the reverse
guard's refusal was audited as an authorized run; a withheld attempt was invisible on the agent's surface; the
guard refused legitimate work (mirror mounts, a root host path, a nested container path); `selectionFor` took its
state from the wrong candidate; the guard's mapping read failed unaudited; two redaction compositions were
non-monotone; a scheme-less credential-shaped argv[0] rendered its password; Docker's listing order could decide the
target; and — found twice, independently — the withheld notice interpolated a raw argv element, a leak the previous
fix had introduced. Six of those were the same failure mode: a fix applied to one surface and not its mirror, which
is why the segment predicate now exists exactly once (`isAtOrUnder`/`isSamePath`) and every rendering goes through
one enforced function.

REMAINING (recorded, none blocking; a scoped follow-up task)
The 23 items in `.kata/tasks/routing-hardening/wiki/` include one regression introduced by the last nit fix
(`hostToContainer` with a root host path), two documentation sentences that overstate the residual redaction scope,
the unknown-verb diagnostic interpolating raw input, a bare `host-exec` counting as an attempt, `tsconfig` not
covering `tests/**`, and the docs still pinning `@devcontainers/cli@0.88.0` while the host resolves 0.89.0. None
affects the behaviours above.
